sentences.text:
THESE MFAs HAVING BEEN HEARD AND RESERVED FOR JUDGMENT ON 31.02.2023, COMING ON FOR PRONOUNCEMENT OF JUDGMENT THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:-
 JUDGMENT
These two appeals filed under Section 173 (1) of the M.V.Act is by respondent No.2/Insurance company challenging the common judgment and award in MVC.No.123/2014 and MVC.No.120/2014 respectively.
2. For the sake of convenience the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.

3. While MVC.No.123/2014 is filed by Moulasab with regard to the personal injury suffered by him in the motor vehicle accident dated 13.11.2013, MVC.No.120/2014 is filed by the said Moulasab and his wife Reshma regarding the death of their son Mohammed Haneef in the said accident.
4. FACTS:

It is the case of the petitioners that on 13.11.2013, at 11.30 a.m., petitioner Moulasab and his son i.e., deceased Mohammed Haneef were proceeding on motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-36/W-5283 (motor cycle for short) on Hunasagi-Kembhavi Main road.

When they were near Hunasagi, rider of motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-33/L-7205 (offending vehicle for short)
came from opposite side in a rash or negligent manner and dashed against motor cycle.
Due to the impact, both Moulasab and Mohhamed Haneef sustained grievous injuries.
Mohammed Haneef died at around 2.00 p.m. while Moulasab sustained grievous injuries
4.1 Petitioner Moulasab has contended that he was a tailor by profession and earning Rs.10,000/- p.m.
After the accident, he is unable to work as he used to and as such suffered loss of income.
So far as MVC.No.120/2014 is concerned, petitioners have pleaded that at the time of accident, deceased Mohammed Haneef was aged 18 years.
He was studying in II PUC and at the same time working as a mechanic at Al-noor Generator Service Centre, Yadgir and earning Rs.6,000/-p.m.
Respondent No.1 being the owner- cum-rider of the offending vehicle and respondent No.2 being the insurer are liable to pay the compensation.
5. Respondent No.1 has appeared through counsel, but did not chose to file written statement.

6. Respondent No.2 has filed written statement denying the age, occupation, the income of the petitioner Moulasab and also the age of deceased Mohammed Haneef and that he was doing mechanic work and earning Rs.6,000/- p.m. Respondent No.2 has disputed that accident occurred due to the rash or negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent No.1.
7.

On the other hand respondent No.2 has taken up a specific defence that it was petitioner Moulasab who was also responsible for causing the accident and as such to the extent of his The Icici Lombard vs Reshma W/O Moulasab Nadaf And Ors on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14020731/
3 contribution towards the accident, the compensation may be reduced.

At the time of accident,
respondent No.1 was not holding a valid driving license and as such it is not liable to pay the compensation and prays to dismiss the petition.
8. Based on these pleadings, the Tribunal has framed necessary issues.
9. In MVC.No.120/2014, petitioner No.2 is examined as PW-1 and one witness as PW-2 and Ex.P1 to 8 are marked.
10. On behalf of respondent No.2, RW-1 is examined and one witness is examined as RW-2.
Ex.R1 to 3 are marked.
11. In MVC.No.123/2014, petitioner Moulasab has examined himself as PW-1 and one witness as PW-2.
Ex.P1 to 8 are marked.
12. On behalf of respondent No.2, RW-1 is examined and Ex.R4 is marked.
13. Vide impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petitions granting compensation in a sum of Rs.2,50,000/- in MVC.No.123/2014 as detailed below:

Heads Amount  In Rs.
 Loss of future income 2,01,600  Loss of amenities & comforts 20,000  Pain and sufferings and 21,000  mental agony  Food, nourishment and 8,000  conveyance charges  TOTAL 2,50,000 14.
Similarly in MVC.No.120/2014, the Tribunal has granted compensation in a sum of Rs.7,28,000/- and directed respondent No.2 to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a as detailed below:

Heads Amount  In Rs.
 Loss of estate 6,48,000
Loss of love and affection 50,000
Towards funeral expenses 30,000  and transportation  TOTAL 7,28,000 15.
Petitioners have not challenged the impugned judgment and award so far as quantum is concerned.

sentences.text: However, respondent No.2 has come up with these two appeals contending that the impugned judgment and award is erroneous and liable to be set aside.
The Tribunal without appreciating the oral and documentary evidence has fastened the liability on respondent No.2 which has led to gross miscarriage of justice.

The Tribunal has failed to appreciate the fact that petitioner Moulasab was riding the motor cycle without driving license and in fact he is also arraigned as accused No.3 for riding the motor cycle without possessing valid driving license.
Therefore, the contributory negligence on the part of petitioner Moulasab is to be taken into consideration while granting the compensation.

The evidence placed on record indicate that when the offending vehicle ridden by respondent No.1 was coming from the opposite side, it was the duty of the petitioner Moulasab to slow down and allow the said vehicle to over take another vehicle which was plying ahead of it.
Having failed to do so, he has contributed towards the cause of accident.
The petition is not maintainable for non-joinder of the owner and insurer of the motor cycle.
This fact is also not appreciated by the Tribunal and prays to allow the appeal and modify the impugned judgment and award.
17. On the other hand, learned counsel representing the petitioner supported the impugned judgment and award and prays to dismiss the appeals.

18. Heard arguments and perused the record.
19.

In respect of the accident, complaint was filed by petitioner Moulasab, wherein he has specifically alleged that the accident was caused due the rash or negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent No.1.
In fact he has deposed that in the said accident he and his son sustained injuries and were taken to the hospital.
Based on the said complaint, the concerned police have registered case in Cr.No.141/2013.

However, after conducting detailed investigation, charge sheet is filed arraigning respondent No.1 as accused No.1, one Ibrahim Mehaboob Sab Aarati, the owner of motor cycle which petitioner Moulasab was riding as accused No.2 with an allegation that he allowed petitioner Moulasab to ride the vehicle without possessing a valid driving license.

Similarly,
petitioner Moulasab is also arraigned as accused No.3 with the allegations that he rode the motor cycle without possessing valid driving license.
20. Thus, the allegations against petitioner Moulasab is that he was not possessing a valid driving license when the accident took place.
However, there are no allegations that on account of he not possessing a valid driving license, he contributed towards the cause of accident.
In fact in the charge sheet also, there are no allegations that he contributed towards the cause of accident.

Therefore,
rightly the Tribunal has attributed the entire negligence on the part of respondent No.1 being the owner and rider of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, this Court is of the considered opinion that there are no justifiable grounds to interfere with the impugned judgment and award on the ground of contributory negligence.

21. So far the quantum of compensation awarded is concerned, having regard to the age, occupation and income of the petitioner Moulasab as well as the fact that at the time of accident, deceased was aged 17 years, based on the notional income the Tribunal has rightly granted compensation and on the ground of quantum also, the impugned judgment and award cannot be interfered with.

ORDER
